topics.title: SSH Enumeration and Backporting Verification
topics.content: CRITICAL: SSH version banners DO NOT reflect actual patch status on Ubuntu/Debian due to backporting. OpenSSH 7.2p2 on Ubuntu may be fully patched. Scripts: ssh-auth-methods (auth types without login), ssh-hostkey (key fingerprints), ssh2-enum-algos (ciphers/algorithms). To verify actual patches: use ssh-audit tool, check dpkg -l openssh-server, test for specific CVEs. CVE-2016-6210 and CVE-2018-15473 allow user enumeration.

examples.explanation: SSH brute with delay (use with caution)

warnings: Banner version DOES NOT indicate patch status
Ubuntu backports security patches without version change
ssh-brute may be blocked by fail2ban
User enumeration CVEs require specific testing
best_practices: Never trust SSH version banner for vulnerability assessment
Test specific CVEs rather than relying on version

topics.title: SSH User Enumeration Vulnerabilities
topics.content: CVE-2018-15473 (OpenSSH < 7.7): Timing-based user enumeration via malformed packets. Invalid users get immediate rejection; valid users trigger delayed response. CVE-2016-6210 (OpenSSH < 7.3): Similar timing attack via long passwords. Both require specific tools/scripts for exploitation. Nmap's ssh-brute may indicate valid users via response timing but dedicated tools like ssh-user-enum are more reliable.

examples.use_case: Determine if user enum CVEs apply

warnings: Version banner doesn't confirm vulnerability due to backporting
Tools may produce false positives
Testing generates auth log entries
best_practices: Verify with dedicated user enumeration tools
Check actual patch status not just version

topics.title: External Network Reconnaissance Workflow
topics.content: Phase 1: Passive recon (DNS, OSINT, certificates). Phase 2: Port discovery with stealth (-T2, --max-rate 100). Phase 3: Service enumeration (-sV) on discovered ports. Phase 4: Vulnerability scanning (NSE scripts). Phase 5: Manual verification of findings. Use slow timing for external scans to avoid detection. Prioritize: exposed management interfaces, VPN endpoints, web apps, email servers.

warnings: External scanning may violate laws without authorization
ISP may notice/block scanning
Client firewall logs will show activity

topics.title: Internal Network Scanning Workflow
topics.content: Internal scanning can be faster (-T4) since stealth less critical. Phase 1: Host discovery (nmap -sn). Phase 2: Quick port scan (-F or --top-ports). Phase 3: Detailed scan of interesting hosts (-p-). Phase 4: Service/vulnerability scanning. Prioritize: Domain Controllers (88,389,445), file servers (445), databases (1433,3306), web apps (80,443), management (22,3389,5985).

warnings: Still need authorization for internal scans

Document scope carefully
best_practices: Coordinate with IT for sensitive systems

topics.title: Integration with Metasploit
topics.content: Metasploit imports Nmap XML directly. In msfconsole: db_nmap runs Nmap and auto-imports. db_import loads existing XML. hosts/services commands query imported data. vulns shows vulnerability correlations. Workflow: Nmap discovery → Import to MSF → Search exploits → Validate → Exploit. Use workspaces to organize different engagements.
warnings: Metasploit DB requires PostgreSQL setup
Large imports may be slow
Keep workspaces organized
best_practices: Import all Nmap scans for correlation

topics.title: Active Directory Enumeration
topics.content: Identify DCs via DNS (nslookup -type=srv _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.domain), port 88 (Kerberos), or 389 (LDAP). Key ports: 88 (Kerberos), 389/636 (LDAP/S), 445 (SMB), 464 (Kpasswd), 3268/3269 (Global Catalog). Use ldap-rootdse for domain info, smb-os-discovery for computer accounts, smb-enum-users for domain users if null sessions allowed.
warnings: Kerberos enumeration may trigger alerts
Heavy AD scanning detected by SIEM
Some scripts need valid credentials

topics.title: Ubuntu/Debian Backporting Explained
topics.content: CRITICAL CONCEPT: Ubuntu and Debian backport security patches to older package versions WITHOUT changing the version number. OpenSSH 7.2p2 on Ubuntu 16.04 may have ALL security patches applied despite showing an 'old' version. This causes massive false positives in vulnerability scanners that rely on version banners. NEVER report vulnerabilities based solely on version numbers for Debian-based systems. Verification required: dpkg -l <package>, apt-cache policy <package>, or check Ubuntu Security Notices.

examples.explanation: Check actual installed package version with patch level
examples.use_case: Verify OpenSSH patch status on target

warnings: Version banners are UNRELIABLE on Ubuntu/Debian
Scanners report massive false positives
Must verify each 'vulnerability' finding
RHEL/CentOS also backport but differently
best_practices: NEVER report version-based vulns without verification
Use dpkg -l on target if you have access

topics.title: Version Banner vs Actual Patches
topics.content: Version banners reflect upstream version, not security status. Examples: OpenSSH 7.2p2 banner on Ubuntu 18.04 has CVE-2016-6210 patched. Apache 2.4.29 on Ubuntu has CVE-2021-41773 patched. PHP 7.2.24 on Debian has numerous CVEs patched. Verification methods: Package manager queries (dpkg, rpm), security tool outputs (ssh-audit, testssl.sh), vendor security advisories, manual CVE testing.

warnings: Never trust version alone for vulnerability status
Automated scanners produce many false positives
Manual verification essential for accurate reporting

topics.title: Common False Positive Examples
topics.content: OpenSSH on Ubuntu: Banner shows 7.6p1, scanner reports CVE-2018-15473 - VERIFY with ssh-audit, likely patched. Apache on Debian: Banner shows 2.4.25, scanner reports CVE-2021-41773 - CHECK dpkg -l apache2, likely patched. PHP on Ubuntu: Banner shows 7.2, scanner reports dozens of CVEs - VERIFY with php -v and apt-cache policy. OpenSSL: Banner shows 1.1.1, scanner reports Heartbleed - VERIFY version carefully, Heartbleed affects 1.0.1-1.0.1f only.

topics.title: Verification Tools and Techniques
topics.content: ssh-audit: Comprehensive SSH analysis - algorithms, key exchange, actual CVE status beyond banners. testssl.sh: Deep SSL/TLS testing - all vulnerabilities, cipher analysis, certificate issues. nuclei: Template-based vulnerability verification. Manual testing: netcat/telnet for banner grabbing, curl for HTTP, openssl s_client for TLS. Package verification: dpkg -l (Debian), rpm -qa (RHEL), requires target access.
warnings: Some verification tools may crash services
nuclei templates vary in accuracy
Manual testing takes time but is most reliable
best_practices: Prefer detection over exploitation when possible
